newsitem.title: USA: ONE DEAD, FOUR INJURED, 26,000 LOST POWER IN MASS.. [CORRECTED 13:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ONE DEAD, FOUR INJURED, 26,000 LOST POWER IN MASS.. [CORRECTED 13:27 GMT]

text.p: A series of underground explosions killed one worker, injured four others and left 26,000 utility customers without power for several hours in Cambridge, officials said Friday.

Commonwealth Electric, a subsidiary of Commonwealth Energy System spokesman Peter Dimond said power was restored earlier Friday to most of the utility's customers in the city that is home to Harvard University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and hundreds of high-tech firms.
"There are still repairs to be made," Dimond said, adding investigators and Occupational Health and Safety Administration officials were continuing their probe.
Two manhole blasts occurred Thursday evening, the third early Friday.

Dimond said the four employees were working to fix a cable wiring problem caused by a blast at 1745 EDT (corrects from 0545 EDT) (2145 GMT) in a manhole, when the second explosion occurred. One worker, Douglas Polander, was killed by the second blast. The three other workers and a police officer were injured.
